groups.text: It is currently a clear morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 19 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Paris Saint-Germain has reached an agreement with FC Barcelona to sign Ferran Torres for an estimated fifty million euros. The twenty-six-year-old forward is best known for scoring the winning goal for Spain in the final of the most recent World Cup. Separately, PyTorch has released a technical update that introduces a new way for mark kernels to discover nodes within a scope. This change adds a handler that records each node when CUPTI announces its creation, providing an alternative to the shared subscriber-callback registry. The update addresses specific performance limitations of the previous dependent-edge walk, which suffered from quadratic costs in nesting depth and failed to record scopes entered before a stream began capturing. By utilizing this new backend via the torch cuda graph configuration, developers can reduce annotation overhead from seventy-three point six milliseconds down to thirty-three point five milliseconds.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost around 1,464,440 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,470 casualties suffered over the past day alone, alongside massive losses in tanks and aircraft. While Ukraine maintains operational secrecy regarding its own numbers, a January report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated Ukrainian casualties between 500,000 and 600,000 through December 2025. Elsewhere, Pakistan is celebrating 79 years of independence with gun salutes in Islamabad and provincial headquarters. President Asif Ali Zardari called for unity and reforms, noting that the nation's security remains linked to peace in its neighborhood. In a different sphere, Paris Saint-Germain has reached an agreement with Barcelona to sign forward Ferran Torres. The Spanish player, who scored the winner in the World Cup final, is expected to join the European champions for approximately 50 million euros.

North Korea has denounced upcoming United States and South Korea military drills as a provocation that pushes the world toward nuclear war. A spokesperson for North Korea’s Foreign Ministry claims cooperation between the U.S., Japan, and South Korea is becoming a nuclear alliance, promising a new level of deterrent in response. The Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises begin August 17 and will focus on countering drones, cyberattacks, and GPS disruption. This geopolitical tension contrasts with the immediate violence in Ukraine, where Russian airstrikes, drone attacks, and artillery shelling wounded 14 civilians in the Kherson region over the last 24 hours. Regional head Oleksandr Prokudin reports damage to six high-rise buildings and 13 private homes. Meanwhile, in Germany, a bizarre dynamic is unfolding three weeks before elections in Saxony-Anhalt. The AfD and BSW are fighting for the same pro-Russian, east-German electorate, complicating tactical voting strategies used by the SPD and Greens.

Microsoft is streamlining Copilot to move toward a superapp model, merging its consumer application with the version for Microsoft 365. This cleanup removes underused features, including the mascot Mico, while allowing users to access Office software and cloud documents through a single interface. While tech giants refine their tools, governments are addressing the human side of digital platforms. In Malaysia, the Gig Workers Act took effect in April 2026, providing contractual frameworks and mandatory injury insurance for 1.64 million workers. This legislative shift contrasts with the fragmented nature of corporate data across other regions. For example, Nigerian startup Fylings is tackling this gap by consolidating official company registry data from 18 African countries into one searchable layer. Founded by Precious Okeke under Mansa Labs, the platform provides intelligence on beneficial ownership and sanctions screening to replace manual searches in broken national systems.

US sailors aboard the aircraft carrier USS Lincoln report dire conditions and supply issues while supporting the war in Iran. The ship has spent a record 260 uninterrupted days at sea, leading to declining mental health and reports of some crew members attempting to throw themselves overboard. To address this, the Pacific-based USS George Washington is currently en route to replace the vessel. In separate technical updates, PyTorch developers are classifying higher-order namespaces alongside OpOverload targets. This change ensures that fusion does not pass split views with widened row strides into HigherOrderOperator targets, such as user Triton kernel wrappers, which may require contiguous inputs. Meanwhile, a new commit for llama.cpp clarifies the output logging of target layer IDs. The update makes these logs easier to read by removing redundant timestamps from the extracted layers list.

New Zealand has broken rank with Oceania's football governing body to withdraw support for FIFA president Gianni Infantino. This follows a loss of backing from the Asian Football Confederation, Concacaf, and UEFA over Infantino's failed plans to sell twenty percent of World Cup commercial rights to private investors. While Caf and Conmebol still back him for a fourth term, New Zealand joins nations like England and Norway in opposing his re-election. In France, a retrospective looks at Marine Le Pen’s 2011 takeover of the Front National from her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, as she sought to move the party away from antisemitic controversies. Meanwhile, researchers in Munich and Stockholm found that a single compound could block the lifelong social costs of early adversity in mice. The drug prevented traumatized mice from falling to the bottom of social hierarchies, but only if administered during the trauma itself.

Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries have triggered a fuel crisis in Abkhazia, where petrol stations are seeing queues as far as the eye can see. To resolve the shortage, Abkhazia has begun buying petrol from Georgia, an unorthodox move given the unresolved conflict between the two. Tbilisi describes these deliveries as private business matters rather than government actions. In India, the Meghalaya Cabinet approved a draft resolution opposing all uranium mining and related activities within the state. Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma says this will formally place the state's opposition before the central government during the Assembly's autumn session starting August 24. Meanwhile, a charterer has issued an open letter criticizing global shipbrokers for operating like eighteenth-century cavemen. The charterer claims that closed international networks force cargo owners to use low-tier local middlemen, resulting in generic quotes and lost deals.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain clear with temperatures between 27 and 31 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays all day, Tobias Berlin at ten in the morning, and Höfische at seven in the evening. Your work calendar has a NAS Brainstorm at one in the afternoon.
Mail worth checking: Amazon sent a notification that your SodaStream order is arriving today.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
